- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–8% in next 5–7 days if sentiment turns neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >75 and true outcome drops below 70, adjust downward by 5–10% for next 10d horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes; use “sentiment-weighted average” to interpolate between recent highs/lows.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 1.00 (strong bullish) followed by 0.00 (bearish), model often fails to anticipate reversal; reduce forecast by 5–10% in 3–5 days after sentiment shift.
